nodes.label: The caller fetches, the sidecar cleans
nodes.rationale: The sidecar never opens an outbound connection, because all web access must funnel through retrieval-service so credits and caching are counted in exactly one place. Two doors to the internet would make the counting a lie. Consequently UNREACHABLE, ROBOTS_DENIED and TOO_LARGE are only visible at fetch time, in Java.

nodes.label: MIN_TEXT_CHARS = 200 paywall heuristic
nodes.rationale: A successful fetch that yields almost no article is nearly always a paywall teaser, cookie wall or JS-only page. Naming it PAYWALLED rather than returning empty text stops a blank 'OK' document sailing into the pipeline and failing confusingly during fact-checking. Sharp edge: a genuine 194-character article is mislabelled.

nodes.label: camelCase publishedAt across the language wall
nodes.rationale: Python would normally write published_at, but the reply field is camelCase on purpose so it maps onto the Java record field-for-field with zero configuration. Jackson matches case-sensitively, so renaming it would deserialize as null forever with no error - a near-miss that already happened in Session 10.

nodes.label: Echoing the URL back in the reply
nodes.rationale: Looks redundant but is not: the service is stateless, so a caller firing several extractions at once needs the echoed URL to match each answer to its question.

nodes.label: Dockerfile layer ordering (requirements before code)
nodes.rationale: Installing libraries is slow and copying one Python file is instant, so copying requirements.txt first means a rebuild only re-runs pip when the library list actually changed. Flip the order and every code edit re-downloads all three libraries.

nodes.label: --host 0.0.0.0 vs loopback
nodes.rationale: uvicorn defaults to 127.0.0.1, which inside a container means invisible from outside, so the port mapping would knock on a door with nobody behind it. Worst of all the healthcheck runs INSIDE the container, so the dashboard would report healthy while every external caller got connection refused.

nodes.label: Healthcheck as a Python one-liner
nodes.rationale: python:3.12-slim ships without curl, so the check uses the one tool the image definitely has. /health checks nothing deliberately - if the process is wedged it cannot answer, and the silence is the signal. There is no restart policy on any service: unhealthy is a label, not an ambulance.

nodes.label: pydantic validation (HTTP 422 before our code)
nodes.rationale: FastAPI wires the check from the type hint on the handler; wrong-shaped JSON is refused with a field-by-field explanation and the handler never runs. It is the same job Jackson plus Spring do at the Java front doors.

nodes.label: Sidecar statelessness
nodes.rationale: No database, cache, files or memory of previous requests, so there is nothing to clean up and nothing to roll back after a failure - all the mess lives on the caller's side of the wall.
